recommended.variant: WAI-ARIA role img (not an APG pattern, so there is no APG page). For a meaningful inline SVG icon, use role=img with a non-empty aria-label and focusable=false; for a decorative icon, use aria-hidden=true with focusable=false and no role. Name an icon-only link or button on the interactive parent and hide its SVG child.

entries.behavior: WAI-ARIA defines img as a container for elements that form one image; the role requires an accessible name, permits an author-provided name such as aria-label, and makes descendants presentational.
entries.decision: Give every meaningful inline SVG role=img and a non-empty aria-label so its paths are treated as one named image.

entries.behavior: WAI-ARIA defines aria-hidden=true as removing an element and its descendants from the accessibility API, and prohibits its use on focusable elements or their ancestors.
entries.decision: Hide decorative SVGs with aria-hidden=true, keep them out of the tab order, and never hide a focusable icon.

entries.behavior: The inline SVG with role=img and aria-label announced its name and image role; the aria-hidden=true decorative SVG was skipped while its adjacent visible text was announced. These historical results do not certify current NVDA or Chrome.
entries.decision: Use role=img plus aria-label for meaningful icons and aria-hidden=true for decorative icons.

entries.behavior: The role=img and aria-label pattern announced the SVG name twice, whereas title-only SVG failed; the decorative aria-hidden=true SVG was skipped. The name remains available, but the duplicate speech is a historical Firefox quirk.
entries.decision: Prefer the explicit ARIA name over title-only naming and retain real regression checks for duplicate announcement.

entries.behavior: An SVG with an accessible name but no explicit role was omitted from NVDA browse mode even though Firefox exposed a diagram with that name; Chrome and Edge exposed it as a graphic. The issue remains open and was reproduced with a current NVDA alpha on 2026-08-05, so an explicit role is required rather than relying on title or aria-label alone.
entries.decision: Always set role=img on meaningful inline SVG; do not treat an accessible name without an explicit role as sufficient.

entries.behavior: JAWS announced the inline SVG name and image role for role=img with aria-label and skipped the decorative aria-hidden=true SVG. These are historical results, not a current JAWS support certification.
entries.decision: Use the explicit ARIA role/name pair for meaningful icons and aria-hidden=true for decorative icons.

entries.behavior: JAWS did not expose the SVG image role or accessible name in arrow navigation or the graphics quick-navigation key, although Insert+Ctrl+G listed it; the linked fixture also failed with JAWS 2019/Firefox 76. The issue was closed on 2024-03-31 with a request to reopen if reproduced in JAWS 2024, not with a recorded fix verification.
entries.decision: Keep the explicit role and name, avoid title-only naming, and record the historical Firefox navigation limitation rather than claiming current JAWS support.

entries.behavior: VoiceOver announced the inline SVG name and image role for role=img with aria-label and skipped the decorative aria-hidden=true SVG; the older macOS 10.12.6/Safari 11 pairing failed the same naming pattern. Current real VoiceOver verification remains pending.
entries.decision: Retain role=img plus aria-label and aria-hidden=true, and verify current Safari speech in the real VoiceOver lane.

entries.behavior: WebKit previously exposed a labeled inline SVG with no accessible descendants as an empty AXGroup; the resolved change exposes it as a labeled AXImage, while unlabeled equivalents remain ignored. This explains the older WebKit group-role quirk but does not replace current VoiceOver testing.
entries.decision: Expose one explicitly named image for meaningful SVG and hide decorative SVG rather than relying on implicit group mappings.

entries.behavior: VoiceOver iOS announced the name and image role for role=img with aria-label and skipped the decorative aria-hidden=true SVG, while title-only SVG failed in the same historical fixture. Current touch exploration and reading-order verification remain pending.
entries.decision: Use aria-label instead of title-only naming and verify current iOS behavior in the real VoiceOver lane.

entries.behavior: TalkBack announced the inline SVG name and image role for role=img with aria-label and skipped the decorative aria-hidden=true SVG while preserving the adjacent visible text. These historical results do not certify current TalkBack.
entries.decision: Use explicit image semantics for meaningful icons and hide decorative icons from the accessibility tree.

entries.behavior: Narrator announced the inline SVG name and image role for role=img with aria-label and skipped the decorative aria-hidden=true SVG. This is a legacy pre-Chromium Edge result and does not establish current Narrator behavior.
entries.decision: Keep the same explicit naming and hiding contract for the secondary Narrator lane, with no current-support claim from the legacy result.

entries.behavior: The measured fixture documents extra SVG focus stops in legacy IE/Edge: focusable=false prevents double focus inside links and buttons and prevents a decorative SVG from receiving focus. aria-hidden alone does not repair keyboard focusability.
entries.decision: Set focusable=false on both meaningful and decorative inline SVGs, and never use aria-hidden as a substitute for focus management.
